# Compose Specification support

<!-- Generated by test/e2e/compose_spec.py --doc. Edit CASES there, not this file. -->

d2k runs the real `docker compose` CLI (and Portainer's compose library) unchanged: compose reads the
compose file on the client and sends d2k Docker Engine API calls, which d2k translates to Kubernetes.
Every attribute of the [Compose Specification](https://github.com/compose-spec/compose-spec) is
listed here, and `test/e2e/compose_spec.py` checks each row against a cluster: an attribute either
works, or `docker compose up` warns or fails. None is dropped silently.

- **Supported**: translated to Kubernetes.
- **Partial**: translated, with the limits noted; the rest warns.
- **Not supported**: `docker compose up` warns (the setting is ignored) or fails.
- **Compose**: handled by compose on the client; d2k sees its effect.

## Services

| Attribute | Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | Supported |  |
| `command` | Supported | Becomes the container's `args`. |
| `entrypoint` | Supported | Becomes the container's `command`. |
| `environment` | Supported |  |
| `env_file` | Compose | Read by compose; arrives as `environment`. |
| `working_dir` | Supported |  |
| `user` | Partial | Numeric `uid[:gid]` becomes `runAsUser`/`runAsGroup`. User names need the image's `/etc/passwd`, which Kubernetes does not read: they are ignored with a warning. |
| `user.name` | Partial | See `user`. |
| `tty` | Supported |  |
| `stdin_open` | Supported |  |
| `stop_grace_period` | Supported | Becomes `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`. |
| `stop_signal` | Not supported | Kubernetes always stops containers with SIGTERM. |
| `init` | Not supported | Kubernetes has no init process injection. |
| `healthcheck` | Partial | Becomes a readiness probe, which `docker ps` and `depends_on: service_healthy` read. `start_interval` is ignored with a warning: probes have one period. |
| `healthcheck.start_interval` | Partial | See `healthcheck`. |
| `restart` | Partial | Containers run as Deployments, which always restart: `always` and `unless-stopped` behave as in Docker; `on-failure` is restarted on success too, with a warning. |
| `post_start` | Partial | Run with exec once the container runs. Hooks with a `user`, `working_dir`, `environment` or `privileged` fail: Kubernetes exec runs as the container's process does. |
| `post_start.user` | Partial | See `post_start`. |
| `pre_start` | Not supported | Not yet in a compose release. |
| `pre_stop` | Partial | Run with exec before the container stops; same limits as `post_start`. |
| `container_name` | Supported | The Docker name is kept; the Kubernetes name is derived from it. |
| `labels` | Supported | Kept verbatim; also set as Kubernetes labels where the value is valid. |
| `label_file` | Compose | Read by compose; arrives as `labels`. |
| `annotations` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `hostname` | Not supported | Not yet translated: the pod's hostname is the compose service name, which service DNS needs. |
| `domainname` | Not supported |  |
| `mac_address` | Not supported | The cluster network assigns pod addresses. |
| `platform` | Not supported | The node's container runtime picks the image platform. |
| `pull_policy` | Compose | Compose decides whether to pull; d2k's pull is a no-op and the kubelet pulls the image (`IfNotPresent`). |
| `pull_refresh_after` | Compose | As `pull_policy`. |
| `profiles` | Compose |  |
| `extends` | Compose |  |
| `attach` | Compose |  |
| `depends_on` | Supported |  |
| `depends_on.service_healthy` | Supported | Waits on the dependency's healthcheck. |
| `depends_on.service_completed_successfully` | Not supported | Not yet: one-shot services restart forever, so `compose up` waits forever. |
| `scale` | Compose | Compose creates one container per replica. |
| `deploy.replicas` | Compose | As `scale`. |
| `deploy.resources` | Supported | Limits and reservations of CPU and memory become limits and requests. |
| `deploy.restart_policy` | Partial | As `restart`. |
| `deploy.placement` | Compose | Ignored by compose outside Swarm mode. |
| `cpus` | Supported | CPU limit. |
| `cpu_quota` | Supported | With `cpu_period`, a CPU limit. |
| `cpu_period` | Supported | See `cpu_quota`. |
| `cpu_shares` | Supported | A CPU request (1024 shares = 1 CPU). |
| `mem_limit` | Supported | Memory limit. |
| `mem_reservation` | Supported | Memory request. |
| `gpus` | Partial | A GPU limit on the cluster's GPU resource (`nvidia.com/gpu` or `amd.com/gpu`); `all` requests one. Ignored with a warning when no node offers GPUs. |
| `cpu_count` | Not supported | Windows only. |
| `cpu_percent` | Not supported | Windows only. |
| `cpu_rt_period` | Not supported |  |
| `cpu_rt_runtime` | Not supported |  |
| `cpuset` | Not supported | Use the kubelet's CPU manager instead. |
| `memswap_limit` | Not supported |  |
| `mem_swappiness` | Not supported |  |
| `oom_kill_disable` | Not supported |  |
| `oom_score_adj` | Not supported | The kubelet sets it from the pod's QoS class. |
| `pids_limit` | Not supported | A kubelet setting, not a pod one. |
| `blkio_config` | Not supported |  |
| `ulimits` | Not supported | Kubernetes has no per-container ulimits. |
| `shm_size` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `cap_add` | Supported |  |
| `cap_drop` | Supported |  |
| `privileged` | Supported | Subject to the namespace's pod security policy. |
| `read_only` | Supported |  |
| `security_opt` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `group_add` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `sysctls` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `userns_mode` | Not supported |  |
| `credential_spec` | Not supported | Windows only; compose does not send it to a Linux engine. |
| `isolation` | Not supported | Windows only. |
| `runtime` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `pid` | Not supported |  |
| `ipc` | Not supported |  |
| `uts` | Not supported |  |
| `cgroup` | Not supported |  |
| `cgroup_parent` | Not supported |  |
| `devices` | Not supported | Use a device plugin and resource requests. |
| `device_cgroup_rules` | Not supported |  |
| `storage_opt` | Not supported |  |
| `use_api_socket` | Not supported | There is no Docker socket to share: compose's bind mount is ignored and its upload of the client's Docker config fails. |
| `ports` | Partial | Published ports get a LoadBalancer Service. A `host_ip` is ignored with a warning. |
| `ports.range` | Supported |  |
| `ports.host_ip` | Partial | See `ports`. |
| `expose` | Supported | The ports are reachable within the namespace. |
| `networks` | Partial | Containers resolve the services of their compose project by name. The namespace network is flat: networks do not isolate containers. |
| `networks.aliases` | Not supported | Containers resolve by compose service name only. |
| `networks.ipv4_address` | Not supported | The cluster network assigns pod addresses. |
| `networks.mac_address` | Not supported |  |
| `networks.priority` | Not supported |  |
| `network_mode` | Not supported | `host`, `none`, `service:` and `container:` modes: the container joins the namespace network. |
| `network_mode.service` | Not supported | See `network_mode`. |
| `links` | Not supported | Use the service name, which resolves within the project. |
| `external_links` | Not supported |  |
| `extra_hosts` | Supported | Becomes `hostAliases`. `host-gateway` is ignored with a warning. |
| `dns` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `dns_opt` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `dns_search` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `volumes` | Partial | Named volumes are PersistentVolumeClaims. Bind mounts, `tmpfs`, `image` and `npipe` mounts are ignored with a warning: pods cannot reach the client's files. |
| `volumes.bind` | Not supported | See `volumes`. |
| `volumes.tmpfs` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `volumes.image` | Not supported |  |
| `volumes.subpath` | Not supported | Not yet translated: the whole volume is mounted. |
| `volumes.nocopy` | Supported | d2k never copies image content into a new volume, so every volume behaves as `nocopy`. |
| `volumes_from` | Not supported |  |
| `tmpfs` | Not supported | Not yet translated. |
| `secrets` | Partial | Not yet: secrets from `environment` fail. Secrets from a `file` are ignored with a warning: the file is on the client. |
| `secrets.file` | Not supported | See `secrets`. |
| `configs` | Partial | Not yet: configs from `content` or `environment` fail. Configs from a `file` are ignored with a warning. |
| `configs.file` | Not supported | See `configs`. |
| `logging` | Partial | Logs are read from Kubernetes. Drivers other than `json-file` and log options are ignored with a warning: the kubelet rotates logs. |
| `logging.options` | Partial | See `logging`. |
| `build` | Not supported | d2k cannot build images: build and push them, then use `image`. |
| `develop` | Not supported | `compose watch` needs a writable container filesystem and builds. |
| `models` | Not supported | Needs Docker Model Runner. |
| `provider` | Compose | Runs a provider plugin on the client. |

## Top-level elements

| Attribute | Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `networks.internal` | Not supported | Not enforced; reported on the containers that join the network. |
| `networks.ipam` | Not supported | Reported on the containers that join the network. |
| `networks.driver` | Not supported | `macvlan` and `ipvlan` are refused: pods have no Layer 2 attachment. |
| `networks.enable_ipv6` | Not supported | Pods get the cluster's address families; reported on joining containers. |
| `networks.enable_ipv4` | Not supported | IPv4 cannot be disabled; reported on joining containers. |
| `networks.driver_opts` | Not supported | Reported on the containers that join the network. |
| `networks.attachable` | Supported | Every container can join every network. |
| `networks.labels` | Supported |  |
| `networks.name` | Supported |  |
| `networks.external` | Supported |  |
| `volumes.labels` | Supported | Name, labels and driver options are kept verbatim. |
| `volumes.driver` | Not supported | Volumes are PersistentVolumeClaims of the default StorageClass; NFS `driver_opts` select an NFS CSI StorageClass. Other drivers are refused. |
| `volumes.driver_opts` | Partial | `size` sets the claim's size; NFS options (`type: nfs`, `o: addr=...`) select an NFS CSI StorageClass. Others are kept on the volume. |
| `volumes.name` | Supported |  |
| `volumes.external` | Supported |  |
| `secrets.environment` | Partial | See `secrets`. |
| `secrets.file` | Not supported | See `secrets`. |
| `secrets.driver` | Compose | Compose rejects secret drivers outside Swarm mode. |
| `secrets.template_driver` | Compose | As `driver`. |
| `configs.content` | Partial | See `configs`. |
| `configs.environment` | Partial | See `configs`. |
| `configs.file` | Not supported | See `configs`. |
| `configs.external` | Compose | Compose rejects external configs outside Swarm mode. |
| `secrets.external` | Compose | Compose rejects external secrets outside Swarm mode. |
